utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, just briefly, you had -- the Court had inquired yesterday about our motion regarding MM-032. I checked on that, that will be filed on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have some housekeeping matter to do, but we need to go into private session. I'm not quite sure what do we do about the witness while we do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness should be excused. If it's a matter that has to be in private session, I think the witness has to be excused, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the witness -- if you can just excuse us for two minutes, we'll call you back just -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May the witness please be called in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your consideration, Mr. Kerkkanen. Mr. Kerkkanen, you are once again -- I beg your pardon, not once again, but you are reminded that you are still bound by the declaration you made yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Mr. Kerkkanen. We shall now resume your cross-examination. Yesterday we spoke of the text of annex 1, and we reached page 7. Those to say that's annex 1 to your statement. That's the official title. At the very top of this page in B/C/S you state that the law on the ministries of the SAO Krajina provides for the Minister of Interior to be answerable for his work and work of his ministry to the assembly and the government. This quotation has been linked up with footnote 20. And I have a question with regard to this. Did you come across information to the effect that Mr. Martic's responsibility has ever been put to a vote or called into question before the assembly or the government whilst he was holding the post of secretary or Minister of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't come across with this kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page you state that on the basis of order dated 9 October, 1991, units of the MUP could have been subordinated to the Territorial Defence. In reference to this my question is as follows: Why do you state that these units could have been subordinated where below you quote item 1 of that same order where it states that all police units in preparing and executing combat tasks shall be subordinated to the competent officer of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the substantive difference between your question and what is stated in the -- in the report, Mr. Milovancevic? The difference I see is that in the report it says it is subordinated to the Territorial Defence. Your question says the "officer of the Territorial Defence." Is that the difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I will clarify my question. If the text in the B/C/S is accurate, it states or rather Mr. Kerkkanen states that these MUP units could have been or might have been subordinated to the Territorial Defence whereas the order states affirmatively that they shall be subordinated which means that is not a possibility, rather this is the obligation to subordinate them and I was asking Mr. Kerkkanen's explanation with regard to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically because they were not all the time subordinated to the Territorial Defence, I think that I'm correctly stating that they could be subordinated, as this order stipulates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, am I right in saying that this order provides for the obligation for the MUP units to be subordinated to TO where combat activities are involved, be it on a temporary or permanent basis, but whenever there are combat activities involved? I would like you to respond to my question whether this indeed is provided for as an obligation.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as per this order, as it reads in preparing and executing combat tasks, it says they are subordinated to the competent Territorial Defence officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. In item 2.1 below, entitled, "Milan Martic," and the creation of the Serb police in Krajina, you state that the RSK government officially acknowledged that the 17th of August, 1990 marks the beginning of an organised and armed rebellion in the municipalities with the Serb majority in Croatia, and the first armed confrontation between the Krajina Serbs and the Croatian authorities. My question has to do with the text, or rather the text of the Croatian decision to that effect can be found in footnote 22. You say that this is Prosecution Exhibit 1927. However, I don't think we can -- in the text here we can't see the decision itself, so I would kindly ask for the Prosecution Exhibit 1927 to be placed on the screen. This document consists of two pages, I believe that we have page 1 on the monitors now, which states that in the annex the decision of the government is hereby delivered, and page 2 is basically the decision itself, and could we please see the text of the decision. That's page 7892 in the B/C/S, therefore the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mine doesn't seem to have a second page, Mr. Milovancevic. And it's a document dated much later than 1990, unless I'm looking at the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have on the monitors now the text of the decision in the B/C/S though because a moment ago we were looking at the cover page of the English version. I was expecting to have the English version actually on the monitor, but nevertheless let us take a look at the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, since I have heard that you are familiar with the language in which this decision is written, is this indeed the government decision dated 28th July, 1990 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can stop here. It is hereby established that the war in the territory of Serbian Krajina started on the 17th of August, 1990. Item 2, this decision shall become effective on the date of its adoption. And in the top bottom [as interpreted] of the page we can see Zdravko Zecevic. Is this indeed what the document says?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. It's not the decision by the Croats, as you said earlier, but by the RSK government.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. If I did say so, I misspoke. I meant the RSK government decision. In this government decision it only mentions that the war in the RSK started on the 17th of August, 1990, but in your text under 2.1, you state that the RSK government officially acknowledged that the 17th of August, 1990, marks the beginning of an organised and armed rebellion in the municipality with the Serb majority in Croatia and the first armed confrontation between the Krajina Serbs and the Croatian authorities. Now, I would like to know on what basis do you, in fact, claim that this is what the decision states?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically it's an interpretation of this decision, but based also on the other facts we know what really did happen on the 17th of August, 1990. And this document shows clearly that by the RSK government that date was regarded as a decisive date for the so-called state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is there an English version of this order? We are all in your hands insofar as interpreting this document is concerned. And when you read it, Mr. Milovancevic, with all respect, due respect, I looked at the letters written here, I didn't hear any sound that sounds like this letter, this letter directed in here in this document. I'm not questioning your interpretation, I'm just saying -- or your reading, I'm just saying, do you have an English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can be of assistance, it does not appear that the second page got translated for some reason, or else the translation has not made it into e-court. I just checked our binder of hard copies and it's not in there either. For that I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should apologise. I owe you an apology. I'm sorry, because I really did not expect that this decision has not been translated. Since the document was disclosed to us by the OTP, we assumed that there was a translation. My apologies. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, can we conclude that the text of the government decision you're referring to reads as follows: That the RSK government officially established in its decision that the war in the RSK started on the 17th of August, 1990? Is that a fair representation?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the text that follows you speak of facts, and you touched upon them when you explained why you interpreted the government decision the way you did. You stated that Milan Martic, a police officer from Knin, organised barricades on the roads leading to Krajina and Knin in order to prevent the Croatian police from reaching the police stations in these municipalities and disarming them. In reference to this statement of yours, here is the question: Did there come about an armed conflict as these road blockings were erected? And I'm not referring to any specific location.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting, but I'm not sure -- the way the question is phrased, if he's asking for a legal conclusion, the witness isn't competent to answer and it's a determination that the Court will have to make. But perhaps I'm missing the point of the question or the meaning of the question. Perhaps he's asking if there is a document that -- that states that there was an armed conflict. I'm just not sure I -- I can understand that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that Mr. Kerkkanen wrote that Martic had organised road blocks on the roads leading to Krajina and Knin, and set forth reasons for this, I asked Mr. Kerkkanen whether he came across any documents or information to the effect that an armed conflict broke out as these road blocks were erected.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any specific documents, particularly related to these road blocks and thus causing armed conflict. But as the previous document by the RSK government states, they felt that that was the beginning of the armed conflict or war in the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, I hope we have clarified the situation concerning the government decision in terms of the fact that the decision itself does not state in any of its parts that a given date was the start of an armed rebellion. Organised and armed rebellion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hasn't that question been answered already, Mr. Milovancevic? I thought you cleared it up, you said to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, we have received an answer that was satisfactory. However, in his recent answer the witness again spoke of a rebellion when speaking about the armed conflict, and I merely wanted to clarify this in view of his previous answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that in my previous answer I didn't speak about rebellion, I -- I spoke about armed conflict. Or war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to say that the situation was already tense, as Serbs policemen in Croatia had refused to wear new insignia of the Croatian police. Following this incident Martic, together with several other police officers, was dismissed from duty. In reference to this I'm interested in the following: What sort of new insignia of the Croatian police were these that the Serb policemen, or policemen of Serb ethnicity, refused to wear?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say I don't know exactly how this insignia looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: With a reference to this refusal to wear the new insignia, I wish to know whether you acquired the text of a letter written by a group of policemen who were ethnic Serbs from the police station in Knin addressed to General Petar Gracanin in early August 1990?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my recollection, I think that I have seen this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In view of your reply, I will put a further question on this topic. Do you remember that in this letter the Serb policemen expressed their disagreement with the insignia and with the changes taking place in the Croatian police and they were writing to the federal Secretary of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say I don't remember that exactly the content of this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. You go on to say that as of August, 1990, and up until January, 1991, or rather that this period was a formative period for the forces from which the police force of the SAO Krajina would arise. And you also refer to the statement made by Mr. Martic in Politika in July, 1991, concerning the preparations which included clandestine arming of the Serbian population. Do you see this text, Mr. Kerkkanen? With reference to this I wish to know whether in your review of the material you came across any information about the arming of the Croatian police and the new Croatian compositions in late 1990 and early 1991.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are -- it's possible that there might have been in some documents references, to the arming of the Croatian police, but I don't really remember any specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to jog your memory. Would it help if I were to ask you whether you saw the footage and the transcript concerning General Spegelj in January, 1991, where he is talking to the Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia, Boljkovac, they were discussing the arming of these units and what would be done with those weapons?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of this footage. I haven't seen it. I think that I have read some part of the transcript. But as it was not relevant to this report I was working on, I didn't concentrate more on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. With respect to the topic we have been discussing, in the materials you reviewed, did you find an order from the Presidency of the SFRY dated the 9th of January, 1991, ordering the return of all the weapons of the reserve police force in Croatia, all the forces there? Did you see such an order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the edification of myself, if not the Chamber, the return of the weapons from whom to whom, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this was an order issued by the Presidency of the SFRY, that is the Presidency of Yugoslavia on the 9th of January, 1991, on disarming all the reserve police forces in Croatia and returning their weapons to depots under JNA control. And I will subsequently put a document to the witness to confirm this. I am at present just asking whether the witness has seen or heard of such a document.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's possible I have seen it, but I have to see the document itself in order to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we see on the monitor Prosecution document 645? This should be an order issued by Mr. Martic, the Minister of the Interior, or rather the Secretary of the Interior, in which he is carrying out the Presidency decision, and ordering the return of all weapons in the SAO Krajina to JNA control. Let us just see the introduction, or rather the heading of this document. The top left-hand corner, please. Can you tell us who drew up this document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'm familiar with this document, but this is not the document we were talking about, SFRY Presidency decision. It's referring to it, this document is from Secretariat from the Interior of SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. I was about to ask you whether you were familiar with this decision, or rather that Mr. Martic, as the Secretary of the Interior issued this order acting on the order from the SFRY Presidency on putting all weapons back under JNA control. Does this confirm that Mr. Martic issued an order whereby this decision would be implemented? In paragraph 2 of this decision, this is what he refers to. Can we now see the bottom of the document, please? At the bottom of the document it says that the acting secretary, Milan Martic, drew up this decision. Is this correct, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This order has been given by acting secretary Milan Martic. But I have to say that from the same time period there are documents stating that he was secretary, so there is incoherence in using this title.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this document into evidence as a Defence Exhibit if it has not already been admitted into evidence. But I don't have that note.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this is already in evidence as a result of the report. It's cited in the report. It has a different 65 ter number in the report, but it's the ERN number is the same. So it is in the report. It's in footnote -- I believe it's in footnote 55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you happy with that, Mr. Milovancevic? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Kerkkanen, of the fact that on the 1st of March, 1991, there was a conflict in Pakrac between Croatian special purpose police forces and the local police, or milicija?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but I know that there was this kind of conflict in Pakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that on the 1st of April, 1991, there was also an intervention by special-purpose Croatian police against the Serb side in Plitvice when the JNA intervened as it had done in Pakrac? I may have been wrong about the date. It might have been the 31st of March rather than the 1st of April. I wasn't trying to confuse you about the date.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't remember exactly the date, but in the term of March and April, 1991, there was also a small armed incident in Plitvice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, Mr. Kerkkanen, that the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the SFRY proposed to the Presidency of Yugoslavia that a state of emergency be introduced in mid-March, 1991, after the conflict in Pakrac, but that no state of emergency was introduced because the votes in the Presidency were divided?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. I apologise for interrupting but I guess I just don't see the point of these questions in cross-examination of this witness. The witness, as Defence counsel himself has insisted repeatedly, is not a fact witness, he is not an expert witness. He really had a very limited purpose here of bringing forward documents for the Trial Chamber to be able to consider and a mechanism to bring those into evidence. If -- if Defence counsel has documents that it wants to propose or wants to ask if Mr. Kerkkanen came across documents pertaining to certain matters that have not been cited in his report, perhaps that would be relevant. But to ask him simply if he knows about these events, he either does or he doesn't, but I don't see what it accomplishes, given his status as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was thinking of a document issued by the Presidency of Yugoslavia in March, 1991. In view of the status of the witness, I will withdraw my question by Your Honour's leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are given leave to withdraw, Mr. Milovancevic. To withdraw the question, rather. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I withdraw this question, Mr. Kerkkanen. And at the bottom of this page, which speaks of the clandestine arming of the Serbian population, where you quoted Martic's interview for Politika in July 1991, you say two paragraphs later on that on the 18th of September, 1991, Milan Martic as minister, together with TO commander Salvorda [phoen] Dulovic signed a request for necessary ammunition and other military equipment sent to the Ministry of Defence in the Republic of Serbia. In footnote 28 you refer to this document, of course. My question is as follows: When reviewing the documents, did you come across anything to show that this request was granted?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing anything else than -- in respect to this particular request than the request itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you say that the existence of the police was made official by a decision issued on the 7th of November, 1990 by the Knin Municipality Executive Council. This had to do with the founding of the Municipal Secretariat of the Interior, the executive council informed the Croatian government of this decision and requested them to recognise it. With reference to this I wish to know whether you have seen any documents concerning a meeting between Mr. Babic, the president of the executive council, and some other representatives of the Serb side, with a Croatian delegation led by Mr. Slavko Degoricija who was the chairperson of parliamentary committee in Croatia, Josip Boljkovac, the Minister of Interior and Stjepan Pecevski, his deputy. There are minutes of this meeting which was held on the 10th of September, 1991, and they have already been shown in this courtroom. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 1990, not 1991.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I haven't seen minutes of this meeting. I have seen, I think, some other documents about the meeting, but I don't recall seeing minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to rise again, but, I mean, this really shouldn't be a memory test for the witness. If -- I mean, we could just show the document to the witness. It's in evidence and if there are questions to be had about it, then we could discuss it. But I don't -- I'm not sure what's accomplished by testing the witness's memory on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it would be unprofessional of the Defence to conduct a memory test of the witness in this manner, and that's not what I'm trying to do. I'm simply trying to establish a link between the document mentioned by Mr. Kerkkanen, the decision of the 7th of November, and a meeting held previous to the document. That's why I put this question to the witness. And the answer the witness has given is quite sufficient for my purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much then, Mr. Milovancevic. But if you don't follow up on what is contained in those minutes, then we just, unfortunately we don't understand why you raised the question of minutes at all. You know, rather than just saying to him, look, there are minutes in existence that relate to A, B and C, are you aware of that and what you are saying is this and what you are saying is that, then at least we link up the relevance. If you ask and he says he is not aware, and you leave it at that, then we don't understand why you asked the question in the first place. However, you may proceed, and I hope you can -- I hope you can conduct the trial in the manner that I suggest henceforth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My next question refers to this decision of the 7th of November on the founding of the Knin municipal Secretariat of the Interior. The Executive Council informed the Croatian government of this and asked them to recognise this. Mr. Kerkkanen, do you have a document show that the Croatian government recognised this ministry and accepted it?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have this kind of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I put these questions to you, Mr. Kerkkanen, not to confuse you, but because at this meeting a peaceful solution of the crisis was agreed upon between the Serbian and the Croatian authorities, the meeting of the 10th of September. That's why I felt that these questions were important. I will now proceed. In chapter 2.2 entitled secretariat and Ministry for Internal Affairs, you say that on the 19th of January, 1991 the Executive Council of SAO Krajina adopted the Decree of Internal Organisation and Operation of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs. In view of the footnote to this text, could we please see on the monitor the text of Prosecution document 646, please? It's the decree mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the text which is now before you, Mr. Kerkkanen, there is mention of a Decision on Internal Organisation and Work of the Secretariat of Internal Affairs. Is this correct, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this translation of this document reads, "Resolution on Internal Organisation and Work of Secretariat for Internal Affairs." But at the same time I have to mention that there are two slightly different drafts of the same decree, and the second draft or version is Exhibit Number 1960.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We discussed this second version yesterday, Mr. Kerkkanen. I'm interested now in this version, which is the original version. Could we just look at Articles 2 to 14? In each one of these articles is the Secretariat of the Interior mentioned, and the Secretary of the Secretariat? In the last line of Article 2 there is mention of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs Article 3 begins with the words Secretariat for Internal Affairs and this continues through the document 646. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to know how do you determine that this is the original version. The second version, Exhibit Number 1960, is slightly fuller one, and in the end it reads that it's a true copy of the original [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with your reply, Mr. Kerkkanen, is it beyond dispute that the second Prosecution document, Exhibit 1960, is a copy of document 646? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to see both versions before I answer with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Before we look at those two versions, Mr. Kerkkanen, I only wish to explain something so that you can understand my question. I wasn't asking you to compare both versions, but only to tell me, either to confirm or deny, that document 1960 is a copy of document 646. Is that what it says in your footnotes and in document 1960?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's -- that's footnote -- this is something -- I'm not saying in my footnote is a copy of the first document, as I think that is not the exact copy of the first document. There are slight differences between them. Therefore, in order to explain better these documents and any subsequent questions, I would like to see paper copies of these both documents in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We have those available if it would be of assistance. The witness could have before him both copies, if it would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting, but we just want to get direction from Mr. Milovancevic. Where -- how are you proposing to go about this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it would be important for the witness to see these two documents. That's beyond dispute. What I wanted to put to the witness is the following: That on page 10 of the version in the B/C/S, below chapter 2.2, the witness states that the decree on internal organisation was passed and there's footnote 41 referenced here. Footnote 41 contains Exhibit Number 464. Now, below this text the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 464 or 646.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 646, Your Honours. If I said anything else, I was wrong. But before we carry on, I would like to hear the Trial Chamber's guidance whether we should go on a break now or perhaps a bit later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe it would be convenient to go on a break now, and in the interim if the witness could be supplied with the documents that he says he cannot answer without looking at first. Court adjourned, coming back at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may briefly. Your Honour, we did provide the witness with the two different documents. I also took some time during the break to make copies in case it's of assistance if the Court needs it or everybody else needs it if this issue is pursued. I would, however, having had a chance also to look at the two documents myself, object to the form of a number of the questions before the break where it was repeatedly put to the witness that -- that Exhibit 1960 is a copy of document 646. Now, this may have been a translation issue or a manner of speech, but looking at the two documents, it's immediately apparent that they're not -- one is not a copy of the other. They are two versions of a document with differences that are immediately apparent. And so I would submit that those questions are misleading, misstate the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. I think it would in fact be helpful if everybody could have copies of those documents so that what you've just said can also be checked out and also the -- any subsequent questions can be tracked. Mr. Milovancevic, I guess you heard what Mr. Whiting had to say. I may just add in addition to what he has said that you will note at footnote 41, which you referred to before the break, that on line 3, the reader is invited to see more detailed version of the resolution in Exhibit number 1960 so that the witness does indicate that they are not exactly the same. The one version is more detailed than the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that what you have just said should be beyond any dispute whatsoever. By your leave, I shall resume my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do, yes. And it is indeed beyond any dispute because it's there on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, in chapter 2.2 entitled Secretariat and Ministry for Internal Affairs, you start the text by referring to the Decree on Internal Organisation and Operation of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs. On the same page below, you quote Articles 1, 2, 3, 6, 6A, 6B, up until Article 14. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you quoted articles of the Decree on Internal Organisation and Operation of the Secretariat of the Interior, you quite rightly in article -- when referring to Article 1 speak of the Secretariat of the Interior. However, subsequently when mentioning Articles 2 to 14, in explaining these individual Articles you refer to the Ministry of the Interior and the Minister of the Interior. How is it possible that a Decree on the Internal Organisation and Work of the Secretariat should contain texts referring to a ministry, if you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the question. That's basically one of the main differences between these two versions. I regard the first version as a working paper and the second version as one that reflects the -- the original version of the decree. And in the second version, "secretariat" has been replaced by the word "ministry." That's one of the main differences between these two versions. The second difference is that there are more articles in the second and fuller version than in the -- in the first version of this decree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I also mention to you, Mr. Milovancevic, that it seems as if it would be logical to refer to the minister, because on the quoted version in the report itself at page 14 of the English version, Article 11 is entitled states about the minister's responsibilities. Article 12, 13, and 14 deals also with the minister's authorities. And Article 13 says, "The Minister of the Interior shall issue specific internal organisation." It does talk about the minister, not the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the reason why I'm putting these questions is not to catch the witness in an error or an oversight. My question essentially has to do with the statement put for the by the witness contained on page 4 under chapter 1.2, situation in the SAO Krajina. Could I please refer you to chapter 1.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, under the beginning of the chapter 1.2, you state: "According to the statute of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina promulgated on the 21st of December, 1990, the SAO Krajina executed laws, other ordnances, and general acts of the Republic of Croatia and the SFRY." Is that what you stayed there, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since the statute was passed in late December 1990, where Krajina is part of Croatia the Croatian laws applied to Krajina, then this text you've referred to under paragraph -- or chapter 2.2, the decree on the work of the secretariat is in fact in accordance with the statute, because in the territory of an autonomous district, there can be no ministry, is that right, Mr. Kerkkanen, only a secretariat? The ministry exists at the level of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I ought to refer to the establishment of the secretariat of the SAO Krajina on the 4th of January, 1991, and to the declaration about its establishment on the 5th of January where it explicitly states the SAO Krajina excludes itself from the jurisdiction of the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you quote that well? We're talking about the decision and the powers of the Secretariat of the Interior, because that the power of the Ministry of the Interior shall not apply to the territory of the Krajina without its approval, its consent. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I have difficulties to follow you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We will move on to a different topic, Mr. Kerkkanen. In connection with the decree on the internal organisation and work dated 19 January, 1992, that's chapter 2.2, there you quote Article 6(A).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the year is 1991, not 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: It's quoted there and talks about the possibility of setting up special police units in time of an imminent threat of war, in time of war and other extraordinary circumstances where the special police units shall be set up from the ranks of the police and other MUP employees. I would like to know the following: This decree on the possibility of setting up special police units, is it in accordance with the Croatian legislation, with the law on the internal affairs of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were just a while ago talking about the differences between those two versions, and this Article 6(A) is included in this second and fuller version of the decree, and that's basically -- and it states about the possibility to form these special police units. That was not mentioned in the working paper or the first version at all. I think that in this context, it's not relevant whether it was in accordance with the Croatian legislation, because the SAO Krajina authorities at that time, on the 19th of January, 1991, they didn't recognise any more the Croatian legislation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On the issue of these special police units, to have them set up is it enough for a unit to exist at a different location and then this person can say, "I'm a member of the Special Police Unit," whether it is Baklajic's group, Knin training centre, another group?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What is your opinion about it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, I think earlier in the day or even yesterday you contested the status of this witness. He's not giving an expert opinion here. You can't be seeking his opinion on this. He is telling us what is written in these documents, and what is written in these documents is exact -- he's quoting articles from the document. How is he supposed to express an opinion on the documents? Is that what he's called for?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I had in mind the continuation of the text in mind where Baklajic's group and Silto's [phoen] group is referred to, where the witness gives his opinion as to whether they are special police units or not. In view of the fact that he viewed documents concerning the ministry or the Secretariat of the Interior, my question was whether on the basis of the documents reviewed he had formed a certain opinion about it, not as an expert witness though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you must lay a foundation for your question. Don't ask the question when you intend to go back to the foundation a little later. Put the foundation first before you put your question. Tell him that you expressed an opinion on such an issue. Are you able to express an opinion on the other issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you understand my question, Mr. Kerkkanen? In the text below, you mentioned Silto group and Baklajic's group, Lapra [phoen] group, and some other groups as well. You presented an explanation with regard to these groups in terms of them being parts of special police units or not. In connection with your writing, my question is as follows: On the basis of this Decree on the Internal Organisation of the Ministry of the Interior or the Secretariat of the Interior, can you give your assessment as to whether these were in fact special police units?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree stipulates the possibility to set up special police units. And as we know, it's also mentioned later in the report that the order to establish them was -- was -- or the establishment of the special police units was formalised in May, 1991, and these few specific groups you were referring to clearly, on the basis of documentation, identified themselves as -- as a part of SAO Krajina special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As a follow-up to your reply, I was about to ask you, in fact, the following: The fact that some units presented themselves as being part of the Ministry of the Interior, was -- did that alone suffice for them to actually be considered part of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that. Considered by whom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic? Considered by whom, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was merely a question further to Mr. Kerkkanen's answer that these units presented themselves as part of the Ministry of the Interior, and my question was, was it enough for someone to introduce themselves as part of the MUP to in fact be considered to be part of that institution, or did anything else have to be presented in support of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you know, Mr. Milovancevic, the problem I have with that kind of question is that that's a question appropriately to be asked to the person who set up these MUPs, what did he intend to include and what did he intent to exclude? This witness is dealing with a documents and anybody who then case he is a special unit member and is part of it as a result of these documents have been mentioned here? He can only, say, take it on face value. But, however, if there were other factors to be added which are not apparent from the document, only the person who has those factors can tell us, and that's person who formed the unit. Not this witness. This witness is interpreting documents, not the intentions of the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll withdraw my previous question by your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, in Article 6(B) on this document on internal organisation, you state that the following is stated about the special police units: "The Minister of the Interior," and we're talking about chapter 2.2, wherein you quote Article 6(B). In the B/C/S, it's page 10. I'm not sure which page it is in the English version. Chapter 2.2, secretariat and the Ministry of the Interior, Article 6(B), you state the following -- did you find Article 6(B)?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. "The minister of the ministry shall issue a document only the establishment of a special police unit as described in Article 6(A) of this decree specifying its organisation, manpower and material establishment, strength, and the manner of recruitment of units." I have the following question in reference to this: In order for any special police unit to exist, was it necessary for the minister -- Minister of the Interior to pass an enactment setting such a unit up along with all the other elements identified herein?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're doing the same thing, Mr. Milovancevic. I'm sorry to have to do this to you, but again you're asking this witness to interpret the intentions of the person who drew this document. What you have just read out to the witness is not the words of this witness. This witness is quoting an article, and if there are any meanings hidden behind that article, only the author can answer those questions, not this witness. He is merely quoting, sir. These are not his words. This is not part of his report. It is part of his report to the extent that it is a quotation from an enactment. Now, if you're asking him to explain what went on in the mind of the person who passed this enactment, then you are asking for the impossible, unless he has had an interview with that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the provision of Article 6(B), Mr. Kerkkanen, for any unit of the Ministry of the Interior which was termed a special police unit, did you find any enactment referring to such a unit containing all the other elements mentioned here? Did you come across such a document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can refer to the Exhibit number 78. That's the decision of the Assembly of the SAO Krajina to form Special Purpose Units of the police of the SAO Krajina MUP called, as Milicija Krajina, or [B/C/S spoken] of Milicija Krajina on the 29th of May, 1991. So that's the document that is about the Assembly decision to establish these special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You have just mentioned the decision of the Assembly of the Krajina dated 29 May on the establishment of Special Purpose Units of the SAO Krajina, whereas on page 12, which would be the page following the one where the -- where Article 6(B) is quoted, that's the text after the quotation of Article 14, two passages down from there starts or reads as following: "The police forces under the Ministry of the Interior were known under the following titles: Martic's milicija, police; SAO Krajina's police or milicija; and Martic's men, Marticevci." Have you found that part of the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In view of the text of this decision whereby a Special Purpose Unit shall be called the police of the Krajina, I'd like to know whether these names, Martic's Police, SAO Krajina's Police, and Martic's Men, were these the titles used by the Ministry of the Interior or by some other bodies?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names I have been referring to on the page 15 of the English version of my report are names how generally speaking or colloquially these police units were known in the SAO Krajina. These are not official names of the police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. A few passages below this one you say that a report of the State Security of the 4th of May gives an indication about the way how people were hired to the SAO Krajina MUP and the quality of them caused some resentment among local population and TO members. What I wish to know is whether what you say here refers to just Bukovica or was this widespread opinion referring to the entire SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part of the document speaks about this area of Bukovica. That is near Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we see exhibit mentioned -- the exhibit mentioned in footnote 50? That's 1964, and the title is "Subject information about security problems in the area of Bukovica." The document is dated 4th of May, 1992, and issued by the State Security Service. Could we scroll down a little bit, and could you say whether you recognise this as the document referred to in footnote 50?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we scroll it a little bit more down, please? Yes, that's the document I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this document, there is mention of a conflict between a group of military conscripts and two civilians with the commander of the Kistanje security station and an operative of that statement where the conscripts intervened on the side of the civilians using their personal weapons, and they were brought in after this. And then in the middle of this first part, it says that citizens and military conscripts are complaining because -- and they're criticising Lazo Komazec [phoen] because he hired a number of people who did not meet the standards required. In connection with this, is it realistic to say that there was dissatisfaction with the personnel policy of the MUP or was the conflict about something else? Is that evident from this document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's evident from this document. It illustrates very well that the popular feeling of the citizens in Bukovica was that they didn't like the fact that the many MUP members who were hired were owners of private coffee bars and their friends. So obviously, local citizens were not happy about this -- this MUP personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is there any significance in the text that goes on, which says that the military conscripts are threatening to fire on Kistanje, the public security station there? And it says that Milan Babic's people are active here with a view to forming army units. On page 3, which is marked 3816 in B/C/S -- could we see this on the monitor? The last page, please. Can we see the bottom of page 2 and then page 3? It's different in B/C/S. I apologise. In the passage before the last, the penultimate paragraph, it says: "We wish to draw attention to the fact that General Nikovic, while carrying out the duties of commander of the Knin Corps, that he had close cooperation with Milan Babic, making it possible for moves to be made which have proved to be very detrimental." And then it goes on to say: "Meeting Babic's demands, Nikovic made it possible for members of the SDS to attempt to arm themselves in the form of a TO detachment, a detachment of the Territorial Defence of the local communes of Kosovo, Ramljane, Otisic, Cetinje, Civljane, Padjane, Djevrske. This action was prevented by decisive action by Mr. Martic after he was informed of all this by the state security." I have quoted part of this document in order to ask you the following question: Does this not indicate that there were other reasons for the dissatisfaction among the citizens when they criticised the personnel of the police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, doesn't this document clearly state, and I think it's somewhere at page 1, that the reasons for the complaints were multi-faceted? However, the reason that coffee bar owners and their friends are being employed as MUP members is one of those reasons. Does it really matter whether there are other reasons or not? I mean, it doesn't make it incorrect the assertion that the hiring of coffee bar owners was one of the reasons, and that is the only reason that's being mentioned. The other reasons are actually not being mentioned. If you look at page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know, you see at the middle of page 1 the statement -- that the document says "And Krajina and MUP Ministry of the Interior members are becoming more and more frequent in the areas of Bukovica. Causes and reasons of the incidents are multiple meaning," and I want to believe that by multiple, what is meant there is that there are many reasons for these things. But immediately after that they deal with the question of the personnel that's involved that are employed, and it looks like that reason becomes the dominant reason. But it is by no mean the only reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, you go on to speak about the Public Security Service. In the second paragraph, you say that in a dispatch dated the 14th of January, 1991, and submitted to the public security stations of Benkovac, Gracac, Obrovac, Donji Lapac and Titova Korenica requests these stations to submit the number of employees in each station and job classifications. This information was needed so that Mr. Martic could draw up new wage and salary regulations and a new job classification. In this respect, do you know whether regulations on job classification and on wage and salary regulations, whether these were ever drawn up? Have you ever come across these documents?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason for selecting this document and including it in this report was the fact that it was sent by Mr. Milan Martic showing that he exercised authority on the public security stations and the secretariat of the SAO Krajina. Whether these responses to this request or dispatch were sent, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that on the 16th of January, 1991, Martic submitted a message concerning refusal to sign the Croatian MUP statements. Then you quote the text of the dispatch, which says that this is an illegitimate and provocative act. Gross, unlawful, and provocative. Do you know want kind of statements were supposed to be signed for the Croatian MUP?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At the end of this chapter, before you go on to point 2.2.2, saw in his order dated the 14th of September, 1993, Martic issued an order to all members of the police telling them to carry out all their tasks in a professional manner and you add footnote 61. Does this show that Martic was requiring all members of the MUP to respect the law and to carry out all work and assignments professionally?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I would like to see this particular document, Exhibit number 9 -- 1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have document 1971 on the ELMO. It seems that the text has come up on the monitor. This is the text of the order and, yes, it's in English. That's fine. In the second passage, Mr. Martic says: "I therefore order that in the forthcoming period all work and assignments be carried out conscientiously and professionally, with the necessary measure of determination and promptness. Negligence, indolence, look of initiative and indecisiveness will no longer be tolerated. "Anyone who fails to comply with this order or who fails to behave accord wants Rules Of Service will face disciplinary measures and will be severely punished. "The chiefs of public security stations are responsible for the implementation of this order." Signed by Minister Milan Martic. You heard my question, Mr. Kerkkanen.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact, in your question you stated whether this document says that the work must be carried out with respect to the law. The law is not mentioned in this document at all. The document is about to carry out work professionally and in accordance with the Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is respect mentioned, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, were the Rules of Service based on the laws and constitution of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, but I'm not a legal expert, so I can't be specific about this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In chapter 2.2.2, entitled "State Security Service," you deal with the State Security Service. That's page 15 in B/C/S. I think it's 17 or 18 or further on in English. I apologise for not having the precise page number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It's page 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My question in relation to this topic is are you dealing with the State Security Service here which was set up by the decision we have just discussed, the one on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I write in the beginning of this paragraph, "Establishment of the State Security Service was stipulated by those regulations issued on the 4th of January, 1991."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 of the chapter dealing with the State Security Service, you say that Mr. Milan Babic tried on the 1st of August, 1991, to abolish the state security service in the SAO Krajina, but it seems that this order was never executed. What I wish to know in connection with this is, is the reason for Mr. Babic's attempt made clear in his decision?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to see this document in order to answer first this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Prosecution document 106 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please can you scroll down a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: This document contains three Articles. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen? This decision by Mr. Babic's government.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In Article 2 it says: "The president of the government of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina is charged with preparing, by the next government session, a proposal to establish a government agency for national security." I have already asked you whether you consider that this shows what the reason was for the decision to abolish the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document doesn't state the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does Article 2 of this decision oblige the president of the government to prepare by the next government session a proposal to establish a government agency? I think there's no dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the Article number 2 states.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work, Mr. Kerkkanen, did you see a proposal issued by the government for the establishment of a government agency for national security pursuant to this decision?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in your text, you go on to say that "The Federal Secretariat of the interior, third administration," so this refers to the Federal Secretariat, "on 23rd of March, 1992, slashes the SAO Krajina security service." And then you go on to quote part of the text of this report which says that, "The SAO Krajina security service led by Orlovic is basically on an amateurish, hearsay level, and not capable of seriously countering the Croatian Security Service." Then you go on to say that, "One document submitted in April 1992 indicates that the state security service in Knin reported to the State Security of Serbia in Belgrade." I wish to ask you whether you found the document on the basis of which the state security service in Knin was able to submit reports to the State Security of Serbia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the relevance of that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the relevance is that the witness proceeds to say in his text that on the 23rd of August, 1992, Martic suspended the work of the state security department. Witnesses who testified here said that Mr. Martic suspended this service precisely because they sent information to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I then think you must tell him that, that that's what's been said. Put like that in the air is just irrelevant, because he's just saying "a document submitted in April indicates that," and that's all he knows. He knows what he knows from that document and nothing beyond, and if you want to find out that, you can suggest to him other witnesses said so, and if you didn't get that document from those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I only felt it important to previously establish whether there was a document authorising such delivery of information to Belgrade. However, I will follow Your Honour's instructions and put a direct question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do, Mr. Milovancevic, and do it in such a manner that the relevance of your question can be apparent. Why the Court keeps interfering is simply because your questions do not on the face of it appear to be relevant, and we're trying to find out the relevance, which is one of the factors that must be taken into account by a Court when questions are being asked. You may ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, there were witnesses who testified here that Mr. Martic suspended the work of the State Security Service because reports had been sent to the State Security Service in Belgrade. In connection with this, I'm interested in finding out whether you found any document authorising the state security service of Krajina to deliver information to anyone else apart from their own government and their own ministry.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't found specifically this kind of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to chapter 2.2.3, Special Purpose Units of the Ministry of the Interior. In the B/C/S that's on page 17. That's the continuation of the text following the part concerning State Security Services. In the beginning, you state that the Assembly of the SAO Krajina passed the decision to form Special Purpose Units of the SAO Krajina on the 29th of May, 1991, and that in that decision the Special Purpose Units of the police were named Milicija Krajina or, that is to say, Krajina Police. You go on to say that the decision on the application of the law of -- on defence of the Republic of Serbia in the territory of the SAO Krajina, it was decided that these Special Purpose Units of Krajina would form the armed forces of the SAO Krajina together with the Territorial Defence. Did you come across documents which show who was in command of these Special Purpose Units of the Krajina police mentioned in this law dating from August 1991?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's clear from various documentations concerning special police units that they were under -- acting under -- they were under the authority of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In Article 1 of this decision dated 29 May, 1991, on the establishment of Special Purpose Units - that's under chapter 2.2.3 - you quote that: "These units shall be placed under the authority of the Ministry of Defence." That's one article. There is another provision which is quoted from the Law on Defence dating from the 1st of August, 1991, which provides for the establishment of the armed forces of the SAO Krajina. The Prosecution document number 105 contains the following provision: That these armed forces shall be commanded ex officio by the Prime Minister. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Two pages before this particular passage we were just looking at, you speak of the fact that Mr. Babic passed a decree on the forces of the SAO Krajina, and below that is the text I'd like to refer you to, that's the structure of the Special Purpose Units which was made systematic. Did you find that particular passage? That's page 18 in the B/C/S. It's immediately before chapter 2.2.3.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We go back to the beginning chapter 2.2.3, "Special Purpose Units." We read out the text concerning the establishment of the armed forces of the SAO Krajina. Then the next chapter is that Milan Babic passed a decree on the insignia, and that precedes the part of the text that I referred to in putting the question to you. The text starts as follows: "The Special Police Unit structure was also systematised during 1992. Have you found that passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I may be of assistance, it's the top of page 24. And if I could make a suggestion, perhaps indicating passage by footnote number would be helpful. That would speed finding the passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank my learned friend for his very helpful suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In this text referring to the structure of special police units, there is a footnote 85 at the end of it. So in this particular paragraph, you speak of Special Purpose Units, and then you go on to speak of special police. Are you referring to the same forces? Because in this case, Mr. Kerkkanen, we are having difficulties with identifying the police formations of the SAO Krajina. Therefore, this structure of Special Purpose Units, that's the sentence which speaks of special police units. What I wanted to ask you was the following: Does the entire passage refer in fact to special police units that were established pursuant to the decision dating from the 29th of May, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was possible to establish on the basis of documents used in this report, that is Special Purpose Units established on the 29th of May, 1991, were transformed later during 1992 into the special police units and RSK MUP special brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In chapter 2.3 entitled "Clashes over Ministry of the Interior," which is the chapter starting with footnote 86, if you can find it. The title of the chapter is "Clashes over Ministry of the Interior." There you state that the SAO Krajina state security report from 11 June, 1991, informs about the clashes between Milan Martic and Milan Babic, especially regarding the appointment of new SAO Krajina ministers. Based on the documents reviewed, did you establish who it was who nominated ministers and who, in turn, appointed them? To perhaps give you a more specific question, based on the data that the Defence has, the government of the SAO Krajina nominates ministers and the SAO Krajina Assembly appoints them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That at least should be the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the paragraph that follows, you state that Dusan Vjestica was appointed Minister of the Interior on the 29th of May, 1991, thus replacing Martic from that same post, and you go on to say that Milan Martic was again appointed Minister of the Interior on the 27th of June, 1991. Why. Based on the documents you reviewed, were you able to conclude that throughout this period Milan Martic was -- rather, Milan Babic was Prime Minister and the person who nominated Martic for that post before the SAO Krajina Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know on the basis of documents, of course Milan Babic at that time was the Prime Minister, and Milan Martic, who was secretary or minister of the Ministry for Internal Affairs until he was appointed for Ministry of Defence on the 29th of May, 1991, keeping this position less than a month and then being renominated as Minister of Interior on the 27th of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that he was again appointed minister on the nomination of the Prime Minister, Milan Babic?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to see the Exhibit number 91 about his election to the post of Minister of Interior on 27th of June, 1991, in order to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. Your Honour, would this be a convenient moment for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be a convenient moment for the break. And if in the meantime you can make sure the witness gets document 91. Court adjourned. Come back at quarter to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We are nearing the end of the topic concerning State Security Service, Mr. Kerkkanen. Right before chapter 2.4, you state that the state security has particularly focused on the ever-increasing conflict between Mr. Babic and Mr. Martic. Have you found that portion of the text? You go on to say: "In the report of the State Security Service dated 4th of May, 1992, it is implied that the State Security Service has sided with the policy of Milan Martic against Milan Babic." In connection with this, my question is the following: Is this the report which has to do with Bukovica --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure about the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: -- that we mentioned a bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to hear how it is that you explain your conclusion that this document implies that the SDB sided with the policy of Milan Martic, that is to say the State Security Service sided with Martic and against Babic in view of the fact that we saw a document dated 23rd August, 1992, wherein Milan Martic disbanded the State Security Service, which is only a couple of months after this report concerning Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's very well possible. I mean there's no any problem with the fact that the State Security Service was on the side of Milan Martic in May 1992, and the service was later on disbanded by him. Something may have happened in between, after May and before August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The fact that you cite the text, that particular text in footnote 68, which is related to the order by Milan Martic suspending the State Security Service, dated 23 August, 1992, and you quote it, and you say that the former employees of the SDB have even been banned from entering the official premises. This is my question: Not only did Mr. Martic disband the service, but even went as far as to ban the former employees from entering the premises, whereas you state that the service had sided with him against Babic. Is that really logical?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has been asked and answered. This is exactly the previous question, and it's been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I withdraw the question and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We have now reached chapter 2.4 entitled "Local banned groups affiliated with MUP Special Purpose Units." In the B/C/S, that's on page 20. Footnote 92 onwards. In this particular chapter, you state that in addition to -- that at least Sinisa Martic, aka Silt's group, was related to Martic, as well as Predrag Baklajic's group, the Labra paramilitary group led by Milanovic, aka Labra, as well as units at the Samarica training camp. On the basis of which document did you identify some of these groups as paramilitary groups and others as other types of groups?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have referred to the documents in the subsequent chapter on these armed groups that were affiliated with the MUP Special Purpose Units, and I was using exactly same names of these units that these documents are using and the unit themselves were using about themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, my question was why did you identify some of these groups as paramilitary groups and others not? I apologise if my former question was not clear.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't identify. It wasn't my -- it wasn't my decision to identify some of these groups as paramilitary and others not. I used exactly those names that these units used about themselves and are mentioned in those documents I was using when I was writing the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In this text you state, for instance, the Labra paramilitary group. My question had to do with the following: Why is the Labra group a paramilitary group and Predrag Baklajic's group is not? Why did you style one group as a paramilitary group and the other merely as a group? Do you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Question asked and answered. The witness said that that's how they called themselves and that's why he called them that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When you speak about Sinisa Martic Silt's group, he state it became active during the summer months of 1991, and you state literally: "It operated mainly in the territory of Glina municipality." You cite the heading of the report submitted by Sinisa Martic on the 22nd of November which states: "The Special Unit of the Krajina police." Was it only on the basis of this heading, which read "Special Unit of Krajina's police," which was written by the leader of the group, that you concluded that this was a unit which was part of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on the basis of this one document.
