This report, Exhibit number 2018, information about the task of Special Purpose Units in Glina, written by the commander of the Territorial Defence brigade Glina in February 1992, it refers to this -- to this particular Silt's group, stating that a special unit of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbian Krajina or the so-called Silto's group of 75 soldiers." So this document is referring to this same Silt's group and specifically refers to as a special unit of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Before this text of the TO Glina Brigade Command that you mentioned, you stated in connection with this Sinisa Martic's report dated 22nd of November, that this unit considered itself to be part of the SAO Krajina special police. And in the paragraph below, you mention the report of the Crisis Staff of Glina municipality, which states that armed groups could not operate as part of either the army or the police but engage in criminal activities. And Silt's group is mentioned as an illustration, a group which stole five or six automobiles. In view of the different information given by the command of the brigade of TO Glina and the Glina municipality Crisis Staff, did you find any other document which would indicate that Silt's group indeed formed part of the Ministry of the Interior of the SAO Krajina or the RSK?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exhibit number 19267 refers to this same Silt's group that was sent from the territory of Glina to conduct combat operations as part of police forces. So there are several documents that indicate this group being a part of police units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Police units of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's correct. The police units of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter document 668 shown on the monitor, which is Sinisa Martic Silt's report dated 22nd November, 1991. Mr. Kerkkanen, is -- this report by Sinisa Martic dated 22nd November, 1991, you speak of indeed on the monitor where it says "Krajina Special Police," is this the report you had in mind when you wrote down footnote 97?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does this document contain a reference number, a stamp, a signature, or any other reference except for the allegation by the person who authored the document that this was the Krajina police Special Purpose Unit?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question I need to see the B/C/S version of the document. There are no stamps or reference numbers on this document. It's basically a report or operational report written by Sinisa Martic, and -- but there are, as we already were referring to, other documents which corroborate the fact that this unit was a part of the SAO Krajina police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is what you state here now true since you state in your report that the Crisis Staff, in talking about this group, you state then: "In the regular combat report it is stated that on the 22nd June, 1992, Silt's group from the area of Glina was deployed to carry out an assignment as part of the police force. Does it state here that it was deployed as a Special Police Unit or that it was deployed as a unit forming part of the police, or are these two one and the same thing for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. I don't really see how the witness can answer that or, if he did, how it would be -- how it would assist the Trial Chamber in its task. The documents say what they say. And it seems to me -- I'm not sure what is accomplished by having the witness go through and read certain parts of the document and compare it with other parts of the document. That's something that can be done by the Trial Chamber. It can be done in argument. I'm not sure there is anything added by putting the witness through this process. This is something that could be done without the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can move on to my next question. I do not wish to insist, and I accept what has been said. I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to say my objection was more of a general nature with respect to all -- you know, all the questions. I mean, when I object the question gets withdrawn and we move to another question which is -- tends to be similar. I'm just wondering if there could be some direction given to Defence counsel to focus in on questions that really would be -- that really require the witness and not on questions that are simply argument or reading out the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, I think the Trial Chamber has asked you on many occasions to please ask focused questions and questions that really make progress. You seem to be going through this witness's report sentence by sentence and asking him comparative questions. I've tried this whole afternoon. The Chamber is getting tired of interrupting you in your questions because we want to get done the job. Once again I ask you to please be focused, get what you want to get from the witness. Don't try to -- I don't know if you're trying to get contradiction, but if you're trying to go for contradiction, go for the contradiction and get it. But the way you are cross-examining, it really -- the Chamber doesn't see the purpose of your cross-examination to tell the honest true. I don't know how your questions are going to help the Chamber in finding the truth in this matter. Once again, I ask you to please focus your questions to issues that support the case of the Defence or weaken the case of the Prosecution. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At the end of the text concerning Silt's group, you state that this group, as many other groups, took part in criminal activities and that in September, 1993, Milan Martic issued an order to conduct an operation against the group by a special brigade of the RSK MUP with the support of the Knin SUP -- or MUP. Did you come across any documents indicating that this operation was, in fact, carried out?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say I don't remember. It may be -- it's difficult to recall. It's quite a long time when I was reviewing these documents, so I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The short answer is you don't recall. Mr. Kerkkanen? Your short answer is you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The next group you mention, Mr. Kerkkanen, is Predrag Baklajic's group for whom you said he had introduced himself to the commander of the 2nd Lika Brigade as a captain. You also state that Baklajic and his group did not cooperate with the 2nd Lika Brigade and that colonel Trbojevic asked Milan Martic to remove this unit from his area of responsibility. Did this -- or was this Baklajic's group --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Defence counsel please repeat his question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question, Mr. Milovancevic? The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The question was: Was Baklajic's group routed or crushed by the invention of the SAO Krajina or the RSK MUP by way of arresting the leader of the group and several of its members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it the evidence of the witness that it was crushed or routed at all, or is this -- or is this a fact that comes from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked this because of some documents which indicate that the witness ought to know that it was. This was something referenced in the footnotes, and I just wanted to find out whether the witness was aware of this particular piece of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you give me the footnote in order to refresh my memory? Yes. May I continue? I have it here. I had difficulties to find it. It's actually Exhibit number 688 where information from Knin SUP indicates that the -- the Vrhovine police Special Purpose Unit led by Predrag Baklajic was getting out of control, and Milan Martic had to give an order to disband his unit in early 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the order to disband the group, which was issued by Mr. Milan Martic as the Minister of the Interior, do you recall the information to the effect that the Ministry of the Interior of the RSK had conducted a very detailed inquiry into the activities of this group?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a few documents cited in this report and specifically under this paragraph that refers to investigations carried out in relation to this Baklajic group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we see P1419 on the monitor, please? It also refers to a report on the activity of paramilitary groups. In this document, Mr. Kerkkanen, which is mentioned in footnote 115 on page 23, on page 2 it says that in the Lika area the activity of a group led by the late Baklajic is being revived. This group had been routed on the 22nd of February, 1992, and its leaders arrested. If we could find that portion on page 2. Have you found that portion of the text, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't found. Must be on the other -- on the other page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it's at the top of page 3 on the English.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's evident from this document, then, that Baklajic's group was broken up on the 22nd of February, 1992, and that because of inadequate judicial measures and the poor political situation in the Krajina, the members of this group have become active again. The next passage mentions the explanation provided by Mr. Uzelac, which you also quote in your report. He calls this group a Special Purpose Unit of the SAO Krajina. Mr. Uzelac, however, is mentioned in this report along with other information which compromises his integrity. He has been dismissed from the police as a troublemaker. Is there such a report in this -- contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document states that Mr. Uzelac was removed from his post in January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When describing the activity of this group, you say that Major Knezovic from the security organ of the JNA states that this group has been operating almost independently, claiming that they received their tasks directly from Knin. In the report, however, it says that the 2nd Lika Brigade was not successful in maintaining control over this group. All this information about Baklajic's group and its criminal activities, doesn't this indicate that this was a common kind of bandit paramilitary group terrorising the local population? It was just a criminal gang in other words terrorising the entire population?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's, in my opinion, interesting to note that this group was by the Korenica municipality [indiscernible] staff understood as being a group of the SAO Krajina Special Purpose Units in 1991, and as well it's interesting to note that when I was reviewing thousands and thousands of documents, I didn't see a single document from 1991 where Mr. Martic, as Minister of the Interior, would have taken any disciplinary action against groups like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with your reply, Mr. Kerkkanen, in the first paragraph about Predrag Baklajic's group in your report, didn't you say that Colonel Petar Trbojevic informed Mr. Martic about the behaviour of this group on the 13th of November, 1991, and reiterated his request. And in February, 1992, the group was broken up.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there's not any indication that Mr. Martic would have taken any initiative before February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you consider that the Ministry of the Interior and Minister Martic could have taken any initiative before they received information concerning events on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it's -- I think it's beyond the capacity of this witness to answer that question. He's not -- he's not -- he can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question referred to the point in time when Mr. Martic and the Secretariat of the Interior were informed about the problems being caused by this group, and my question was whether the witness had any information that would show that Martic had been informed about this before November, 1991. That was the point of my question. Could Martic have done anything before receiving this information. If Your Honours people the question is superfluous I will withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to know whether you have evidence to bring forward to say that when Mr. Martic acted in February, 1992, it was as a direct result of the complaint of November, 1991. If you are going to ask that question -- if you're going to bring that evidence, then I think the question might just be allowed. But in the absence of that kind of evidence up your sleeve when you call your witnesses, I do not understand the relevance, because -- unless you can tell us that Martic does -- when he did act in February, 1992, it was as a direct result of that report of November. In other words, what I'm trying to suggest to you is, it is not clear whether he's acting because of that report or he's acting because of some intervening report that he may or may have received which the witness may not be aware of, or some observation he made on the behaviour of these people. Does he give the reasons for dismissal?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not insist on this question. I'm satisfied with the answers I have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In chapter 2.4.2, you speak of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apology. 2.4.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You speak of the Labra group, and you say that in some actions they acted jointly with the Plaski group and that they presented themselves as employees of the MUP. Can you tell us what the fate of this group was?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have many documents concerning this group. On the basis of Exhibit number 1419 about paramilitary organisation in the Lika area, it's concluded that this group was dissolved in February, 1992, but it became active again later in the beginning of 1994. That's all information I have about this group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the document you mention, Mr. Kerkkanen, does it say that this group threatened to attack even the corps command, the command of the military units in the area of its activity?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I have to see this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's on the monitor. Could we just scroll it up a little bit. Page 2. Can we scroll up a bit? You can move on to the following page. In the passage before you, it says that the members of the Labra group attacked the 70th Infantry Brigade command, and the text goes on to mention there are other activities. Can we scroll up, please? Scroll down towards the bottom of the page. In the next two paragraphs there is mention of the demands made by members of this group to the military commanders. They asked that certain units be joined to others and so on. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, please? At the top of the page there is a text saying that this group continues to be some kind of independent formation. Did you see any documents about this group which would show that it was a group belonging to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only document I saw, the only documents I saw about this group are these two exhibits, 1419 and -- and 1294, and they don't explicitly say that they belong to the Ministry of the Interior, but this group had joined actions with the MUP units, with the SAO Krajina MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 244, you speak of the unit of the Samarica training centre, and you say that this centre was created by the Executive Council of the Dvor Na Uni Municipal Assembly decision on the 18th of June, 1991. The footnote is 117. You say that this was the training centre which trained Special Purpose Units of the SAO Krajina Police and volunteers from the Territorial Defence. My question is: When the decision was issued by the Executive Council of the Dvor Na Uni Municipal Assembly to found this unit, did Milan Martic, as the minister of the MUP, have any kind of influence on this decision or not?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be very precise, on -- on -- based on documents we have in our -- at our disposal, on the 18th of June, 1991, officially Minister Martic was the Minister of Defence, not the Minister of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Martic in any capacity participate in the establishing of this centre? Do you have any such document or any such information?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exhibit number 1485. I'm referring to this exhibit in the last -- in the end of the last paragraph of this chapter 2.4.4, and this -- this exhibit is from the meeting held at the training centre where they stayed, that they gave absolute support to the minister of the SAO Krajina, Milan Martic. This indicates that they were subordinated to Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Your conclusion that they were subordinated to Milan Martic, does it find support in the beginning of this last paragraph where you say that the unit of the Samarica training centre expressed its will to serve as a SAO Krajina Special Purpose Unit in August 1991? To further clarify my question, does the expression of its will to serve as such a unit indicate that they were not such a unit, a Special Purpose Unit of the MUP -- of the Krajina and that they wished to become one?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation in 1991 in certain areas of SAO Krajina -- I mean, the situation was little bit different in different areas. The earlier report I was referring to in footnote 118, Exhibit Number 2110, states -- I mean, it's a report on-- about the work of the Special Police Unit of the MUP from 18 June 1991 til 7th April 1992 in Dvor Na Uni, and this particular report states that the training at Samarica training centre in the summer of 1991 was carried out by a special unit of the MUP which itself had undergone training in May and June 1991. This indicates clearly that there's a link between the Samarica training centre and the unit based there and the Ministry of Interior in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does the fact that someone was trained in Knin automatically mean that that person was a member of the MUP in Knin? I'm asking you this because Mr. Veljko Kadijevic, the Federal Secretary for National Defence, for example, studied at West Point as a JNA officer. Do you therefore think he's an American officer because he went to school there?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. I think the witness testified it indicates a link, and that's all he testified about, whereas Defence counsel is putting it to him as though he said that he was a member of the MUP in Knin if you train there. It's also, I think, beyond the competence of the witness to testify about this. I mean, unless there's a particular document that the counsel wishes to refer to, but then again the documents really speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic? Do you have a response, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence is checking the information having to do with the units of the Samarica training centre. Apart from the link that has to do with the training, is there anything else on the basis of which this unit might be considered to be a unit of the Krajina SUP? I'm asking this in the light of the fact that this unit expressed a wish to become a Special Purpose Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the question you asked when you asked whether the fact that somebody trained in the United States that makes him an American officer. I think you must articulate your questions correctly and concisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question was: Does the fact that someone was trained in Knin automatically mean that he was a member of the special units of the Krajina SUP? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it not so that the training in Knin is alleged, at this stage it's allegation, that it was set up clearly to -- to perpetrate what is alleged to have been perpetrated by the special units from Knin? And that these people are said to be doing what is alleged to have been done by that unit? How is this witness supposed to know the recruitment policies of the Knin training centre or the Samarica training centre? He doesn't know the recruitment policies. He doesn't refer to them either. He draws his conclusion from what documentation he has saw. He doesn't say he has seen any documentation relating to the recruitment policies. You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In chapter 3, you talk about the developments in 1992 in the Special Police Units of the MUP of the RSK, and you say that in the spring of 1992, the government of the Republika Srpska approved the rules on the job descriptions, job systemisation of the Ministry of the Interior and that Milan Martic issued rules on official identity papers of authorised officials in March 1992. In connection with these documents, I wish to know whether you compared these with the other documents of the other various ministries of the interior on the various Yugoslav republics and whether these documents were similar or almost identical across the board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Relevance? What's the relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance is that we are trying to obtain an answer from the witness as to whether the MUP or SUP of the SAO Krajina, by its very structure, method of work and activity, was a regular police unit in the area where it was active and whether it performed the regular everyday duties pertaining to public and state security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What has that got to do with what happens in other republics of Yugoslavia? What's the relevance of the other republics of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance lies in the fact that the Vance Plan contained a provision that the Croatian regulations were not valid on the territory of the RSK but, rather, the Yugoslav regulations applied. Mark Goulding, the UN Under-Secretary, informed all the warring parties covered under the Vance Plan about these particular provisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You confuse me even the more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I merely wanted to receive an answer to the question as to whether the regulations governing the organisation, the setting up and activities as well as authorities that applied to the RSK territory were similar to or almost identical with the like regulations enforced in the other republics of the former Yugoslavia, because in fact they should have been similar or almost identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, did you investigate these regulations in the other territories of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, not in a systematic manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what you mean by not in a systematic manner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have read parts of regulations from different republics, but it was not systematic undertaking to compare these regulations with those that were promulgated in the RSK in the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may put your question, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, I ask the following: In footnote 34, you mention Exhibit 1899, which is an analysis by Mr. Pavkovic on the regulations governing the management and activities of the ministries of the Republic of Serbia. In the footnote 4, you mention another piece of legislation issued in the Official Gazette, which was why I thought that you were familiar with these matters and that you could help us. This was the -- this was the purpose of my question, but in view of your answer, I will not insist on the matter any further. You go on to report on the Special Police Units of the Krajina MUP. You say in the middle of the page 25 in the B/C/S, this is footnote 122 for the purposes of the parties, you state that in the July of 1992, Martic informed UNPROFOR that the regular police forces at the time had 7.000 members and the Special Purpose Units had 16.000 men. Did you come across the information that all the heavy weaponry, excluding sidearms and automatic rifles, was in fact under the control of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't come across with these kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to say that these MUP brigades, that's to say Special Purpose Police Units, pursuant to Milan Novakovic's dated 27 November 1992, were reorganised together with the Territorial Defence into the Serbian army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. This decision is contained in footnote 129. Since this is a rather longish document did you notice towards the end of the text of this document a provision whereby the complete weapons of the Serbian army thus formed, which included the Special Purpose Units, were found to be locked up and the key in the hands of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to refresh my memory, I need to see the end of this document where it states so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document on the monitor. This is document 1367, the order setting up -- order for forming staffs and units of the Serbian army, dated 27 November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You see that the heading reads "Main Staff the Serbian army. Knin, 27 November 1992." The title of the document is "Re-organising the Territorial Defence and the Special Units of the police into the Serbian Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." Below there is the order. Could we please look at page 17. This document has 17 pages in all, so it should be the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You can stop there. Please take a look at item 6, Mr. Kerkkanen. Item 6 reads: The Serbian Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina shall keep and maintain its weapons and equipment in depots with the presence of UNPROFOR and in accordance with the Vance Plan. Do you know until what point in time were the weapons stored in the depots under the control of UNPROFOR? Did there come a time, in fact, when they were no longer under their control?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm just going to object because unless I'm missing something, the sentence in 6 don't say the weapons are under the control of UNPROFOR. It says they're kept in depots with the presence of UNPROFOR representatives. Maybe counsel's talking about something else, but it confuses matters if the reference is to this document and this section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was: The Serbian army of the RSK, which was formed in this way to include the Special Purpose Units, was it under UNPROFOR's control or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's just the basis of the objection, Mr. Milovancevic, because we don't -- counsel for the Prosecution doesn't understand where you get the word "control" from, because the document to which you referred the witness talks of "in the presence of," not under the control of. In other words, because that word doesn't appear in the document you're referring the witness to, you're not entitled to use the words "under the control of UNPROFOR," unless you want to confuse this witness or confuse everybody else. That's the basis of the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was a misunderstanding. I did not understand the point of the objection, and I -- it was an oversight on my part. The text indeed reads as you put it, and it was not my intention to mislead either you or the witness. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You now understand the purpose of the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to respond to the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the point I was trying to make in asking the question to which my learned friend objected was to refer to the Special Purpose Units and the activities of the organs controlling these units and whether the witness had any documents or knew of any documents that would either confirm or deny such a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are again talking of organs controlling these units. Now, control is the very basis of the objection, Mr. Milovancevic. The word "control" or "controlling" is the basis of the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the presence. I apologise, Your Honour. Obviously I am tired by now, but I was referring to the presence, the word mentioned in item 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like a break, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do believe it is the time for us to break for the day, Your Honour, but perhaps the witness could answer my question and then we could finish with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Only after you have asked it correctly. There is an objection. You have not replied to the objection. You have been telling us what you meant to say, but you keep going back to "control." Phrase your question so the witness can answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In view of this portion of the order, Mr. Kerkkanen, did you come across any documents indicating that this order was not implemented or that steps were taken contrary to this order?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not documents, but I myself was serving in UNPROFOR in 1993, in the area of RSK, and I saw in my own eyes light artillery pieces in the field that obviously were not supervised by -- by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My last question further to your reply. Did this happen after the so-called Maslenica operation and the large-scale operation undertaken by the Croatian forces which was condemned by the Security Council? Is that the time period?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can you be precise about the time period?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That was the 21st of January, 1993, when a large Croatian offensive was launched against sector south during which many people were killed and which was condemned by the Security Council.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was posted in the RSK, more specifically in Knin, from the end of April to the end of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe it is the convenient time for ending our -- today's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Court will adjourn. We will resume on Monday at 9.00 in this court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of May, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
